item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Tanya's triangle $ABC$ has $\angle A=50^{\circ}$ and $\angle B=60^{\circ}$. Side $BC$ is extended beyond $C$ to a point $D$, forming exterior $\angle ACD$.

Which claim finds $\angle ACD$ correctly?

options.A: Find $\angle C=70^{\circ}$ from the angle sum, but stop without subtracting from $180^{\circ}$ to get the exterior angle on the straight line.
options.B: Say that writing $\angle ACD=110^{\circ}$ is what creates $\angle A=50^{\circ}$ and $\angle B=60^{\circ}$, instead of using those interiors to find the exterior.
options.C: First $\angle C=180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=70^{\circ}$; then $\angle ACD=180^{\circ}-70^{\circ}=110^{\circ}$ because $\angle ACB$ and $\angle ACD$ form a straight angle.
options.D: Also use $180^{\circ}-70^{\circ}$ as the measure of an interior angle of a quadrilateral with no side extended, beyond this exterior-angle setting.
